..
Dry conditions continue for all the Marianas with the exception of 
island effect showers possible for all islands Tuesday, as winds 
continue to weaken. These will likely remain shallow and short lived 
in nature due to dry air in the upper levels of the atmosphere. By 
Friday night, rainbands ahead of Invest 96W, currently still north of
Kosrae, may begin to move into the region and bring scattered 
showers and some thunderstorms. By Saturday, heavy showers are 
likely, becoming widespread heavy showers that night as 96W passes 
near or through the Marianas. Heavy showers will likely continue 
through Sunday and possibly Sunday night before conditions start to 
clear out Monday. Gusty winds are expected to begin Saturday as well 
and last through Sunday night. The track and intensity of 96W remains
highly uncertain as the system has yet to organize and is still 5 to
6 days out. Residents in the Marianas should continue to monitor 
forecasts over the next several days, and maintain a general state of
preparedness in case of a potential tropical storm or typhoon. See 
the "Tropical Systems" section for more details on 96W.

Marine...
Combined seas of 4 to 5 feet look to decrease through midweek to as 
low as 3 feet. Swells consist of a dominant north swell from distant 
Typhoon Koguma and a smaller northeast swell. This is causing a 
moderate risk of rip currents along north and east facing reefs. Seas
are expected to increase significantly sometime Friday ahead of 
Invest 96W. Light northwest winds will continue to ease today, 
becoming east to northeast by early Wednesday and gradually 
increasing through the end of the forecast period.

Tropical Systems...
What was formerly Invest 95W is now TD 28W. It's currently located at
16.6N 150.5E, or 315 miles east-southeast of Alamagan. It's moving
north-northwest at 5 mph. Today the center has become more exposed,
as it's displaced from the convection to its south. The latest
forecasts show a gradual turn to the west-northwest Tuesday, with an
increase in forward speed as it traverses the open Pacific. 

Then, we have Invest 96W, which has been quite fickle over the last
18 hours. After robust convective development overnight, it's
convection today has been less impressive. With that said, the 
general consensus is for 96W to meander north of Kosrae/east- 
northeast of Pohnpei for another 12 to 24 hours, before turning west-
northwest as it heads towards the Marianas.

Here's what "we're more sure of:" 96W will pass through the Marianas
as a tropical storm or typhoon. It'll pass somewhere from south of 
Guam to Anatahan. Timing looks to be sometime over the weekend, 
possibly Saturday.

What we're less sure of...where exactly will the track be, what will
the strength be if it is a typhoon.

What can folks do now? October and November is peak typhoon activity
for the Marianas. Now is the time to make casual preparations for the
storm (cut down tree limbs overhanging the fence or call GPA if
branches are near the power lines. Make sure at some point over the
next few days you secure any loose items in the yard. Stay informed,
and stay calm. Continue to follow us on social media, as we'll be
posting at least once a day, with that increasing as we head into the
latter half of the week when we'll probably have someone monitoring
the social media pages ever hour or two. It would be good to check
with your elderly neighbors now and see if they need anything.
Lastly, continue to monitor our forecasts at www.weather.gov/gum

Eastern Micronesia...
All eyes are on Invest 96W, as it's currently meandering north of 
Kosrae/east-northeast of Pohnpei. Winds have increased somewhat today
at both locations, allowing for better moisture transport to interact
with surface convergence. This has lead to locally heavy showers at 
Kosrae where visibilities dropped to 1 mile at the airport, and 
visible imagery shows the monsoon-like developing "inflow" 
strengthening, with showers moving into Pohnpei. As such, rainfall 
coverage/potential was ramped up to numerous (70% probabilities) for 
the next 24 hours, and things were increased some for Wednesday at 
both locations. A Special Weather Statement (SPS) was issued for 
Pohnpei and Kosrae to account for this. Isolated wind gusts to 35 
knots was also included in the SPS, as well as the forecast.

Further east, Majuro will see scattered showers, but heavy rain and 
wind gust potential is lower. heading into the latter half of the 
week and weekend, a drying trend looks to commence at Pohnpei and 
Kosrae, with Majuro potentially continuing to see scattered showers, 
due to closer proximity to the monsoon trough.

As for marine conditions, aside from isolated gusts to 35 kt near
heavier showers or thunderstorms, seas look to be in the 5 to 7 foot
range near Pohnpei and Kosrae, with winds mainly in the gentle to 
fresh range through wednesday, decreasing there after. majuro will 
see mainly light to gentle winds with seas a foot lower
